newsitem.title: CHINA: Quake hits sea off east China,no injuries reported.
newsitem.headline: Quake hits sea off east China,no injuries reported.

text.p: An offshore earthquake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale shook the Yellow Sea near eastern China's Shanghai city on Saturday, but no casualties were reported, a State Seismological Bureau official said.
"Currently, there's no (report of) damage or injuries whatsoever," the official said by telephone. "There shouldn't be any, because it was 100-200 km (60-125 miles) from the coast."
The earthquake struck at 9.56 p.m. (1356 GMT), with an epicentre at 31.7 degrees north latitude, 123.1 east longitude, he said.
There was no danger of any tsunami (tidal waves) from the tremor, which was felt in Shanghai, China's biggest city, and areas of neighbouring Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, he said.
There had been no reports of any damage to shipping in the area, he said but gave no details. Officials of the Shanghai Seismological Bureau were unavailable for comment.
"This earthquake wasn't really very big," an official of the Jiangsu Seismological Bureau said.

Earthquakes are a constant menace in many areas of China, which officials have said lacks the economic muscle to construct truly tremor-resistant buildings and must rely instead on hit-or-miss forecasting to cut losses.
Scientists say China is currently passing through a period of particularly high seismological activity.
In September, a minor tremor injured 17 people in southwestern Yunnan province's Lijiang county, where at least 304 people were killed in February by an earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale.
The February quake damaged more than 1.17 million homes, completely destroyed 340,000, left 160,000 people without shelter and caused huge economic damage, local officials said.
